overview: The Historic District Commission approved certificates of appropriateness for chimney rebuilds at 306 High Street and a new exterior railing at 15 High Street. Consultant Chris Skelly presented strategic recommendations on creating local historic districts and securing administrative staff support for the commission.

items.title: 306 High Street Chimney Rebuild
items.summary: Approved an application to dismantle and rebuild two damaged brick chimneys down to the roofline using matching historic brick and lead flashing.

items.title: 15 High Street Railing Application
items.summary: Approved an application to install a custom steel and mahogany handrail along the front sidewalk steps, with commissioners recommending consideration of a narrower handrail profile.

items.title: Strategies for Establishing Local Historic Districts
items.summary: Consultant Chris Skelly presented strategies for expanding local historic districts, advising the commission to establish local design guidelines, pursue single-building districts, and build grassroots neighborhood support.

items.title: Administrative Staff Assistance Report
items.summary: Chris Skelly reviewed staffing models from neighboring communities to alleviate volunteer workloads and support Open Meeting Law compliance, prompting the commission to arrange a meeting to present the findings to the mayor.

items.title: 78 Cotting Street Public Comment
items.summary: Resident Marianne Adduci inquired about establishing a historic district for 78 Cotting Street, which commissioners deferred to a future meeting pending the drafting of local guidelines and community outreach.
